name: Venusaur
intro: Deep turquoise skin, pink inner ears and large rose-pink flower petals. Distinguish the pale petal spots from green leaves, olive vines and the yellow flower crown. Use only anatomical features clearly drawn; the brown trunk may be hidden behind the head and foliage.

artwork.attribution: Official Pokémon artwork. © Nintendo / Creatures Inc. / GAME FREAK inc. Source: Pokémon.com.

technique: Use an upper-left light source and light pressure (1–2 out of 5) for the first layers. Build transparent layers before medium-pressure blending. Test pencils on spare paper: digital swatches are estimates and barrel colours can differ from pigment. Separate the actual visible outline shapes from background foliage.

steps.text: Lay @113 over the forehead, muzzle and cheeks with light pressure, leaving the upper-left areas brighter. Keep the two inner ear triangles clear of turquoise.
Build @110 through the main head colour, @111 beneath the brow and jaw and @109 in the deepest shadow beneath overlapping foliage. Blend the face with @113.
Colour the inner ear triangles with @050 as a pale base, then @017 and a little @165 along the lower edge. Keep the outside of the ears turquoise.
Apply @113 to the back, flanks and legs, leaving the upper shoulders and the tops of the feet lighter. Keep the claws as bare paper.
Build @110 on the torso and @111 under the belly, inside the legs and behind the knees. Follow the rounded bulk of each limb with light curved strokes.
Use @109 at leg joints and beneath overlapping characters or the canopy. Treat the small raised skin bumps as turquoise skin with a little @111 along their lower edges, not dark blue spots.
If the drawing genuinely includes separate body markings, use @080 with a little @071 at the lower edge. Skip this entirely if only raised skin bumps are outlined.
Lay @130 on the small foreground leaves and broad canopy leaves, keeping the veins and tips light. Do not accidentally colour the large spotted flower petals green.
Use @134 on bright foreground leaves and @121 on the larger canopy leaves. Work from the vein outward and gradually reduce pressure as you approach lighter parts.
Shade beneath overlapping leaves with @135 and use @137 sparingly in the deepest folds. If colouring jungle background foliage, keep it a little darker than the foreground.
Apply @050 lightly across the broad flower petals, keeping the small enclosed spots uncoloured. If this salmon base is already applied, leave it in place.
Layer @017 over the salmon base to make it rosier, then use @027 around petal sides and bases. Test both pencils on paper first to check the actual hues.
Deepen overlapping petals with @165 and use @157 only in the tightest creases near the flower centre. Blend back with @017, retaining some warm salmon highlights.
Apply @023 with very light pressure inside the pale spots. If a spot needs extra depth, touch its edge with @003 and blend gently with @204 so the spot remains almost white.
Identify the small jagged crown-like flower centre if visible. Apply @045 at its pointed tips and @038 on the main area, keeping it distinct from green leaves and pink petals.
Shade the bottom of the yellow crown with a little @040, especially where a foreground leaf partly covers it. Blend upward using @038 while preserving the brightest tips.
If a separate brown trunk is actually drawn, use @172 for highlights, @184 for bark and @186 in the deepest grooves. If hidden by the head or leaves, omit the trunk entirely.
Use @108 as a light base on each clearly outlined vine and its capsule-shaped tip if present, keeping a narrow lighter strip along the upper edge.
Build @140 across the middle and lower portion of the vine. Keep strokes following the curve of the stem so the shading suggests a rounded tube.
Use @132 only along the lower edge, roughly a fifth to a quarter of the vine width, and at overlaps. Fade it upwards with @140 rather than darkening the entire underside.
For rounded tips use @108 as the base, @140 on the lower outer curve and @132 just at the neck where the tip joins the stalk. Preserve a bright upper-middle highlight.
For a visible rounded tongue, lay @050 lightly across it and use @017 at the rear and lower edge. Keep the middle pale to suggest its curved shape.
Fill the cavity behind the tongue with @015 and deepen the corners with @018, carefully retaining the white teeth and a distinct edge around the tongue.
Leave most of the teeth as paper white. Apply @192 very lightly where each tooth meets the gum and a tiny touch of @179 in deep corners if needed; soften with @204.

details.instructions: Apply @019 to the iris and @011 beneath the upper lid, with @203 confined to the pupil and darkest lash line. Leave white sclera and catchlights as bare paper.
Use @050 as a base, @017 through the middle and @165 sparingly at the base. Keep the surrounding outer ear turquoise.
Use @050 and @017 on the visible tongue, @015 behind it and @018 in the deepest corners. Skip open-mouth details when not drawn.
Leave the main surfaces white, shade the bases gently with @192 and use @179 only in a very deep corner. Blend with @204. Avoid yellow on white teeth.
Leave the small markings nearly white or apply @023 with very light pressure, using @003 only at an edge and @204 to soften.

shadows: Concentrate @109 beneath the jaw, around neck folds and behind overlapping leaves and limbs.
Strengthen @135 and @137 under overlapping leaves. Use @132 along the lower edge of each vine and where rounded tips join the stalk.
Use @157 at deep petal overlaps and @040 near the crown base; keep the petal spots and teeth pale.
finishing.blending: Blend turquoise with @113, bright leaves with @130, vines with @108 or @140 and petals with @017. Follow the curves of the forms and avoid hard outlines made from the darkest colour.
finishing.white: Use @204 only at the end to soften highlights on skin, petal spots, teeth or claws. White can make saturated pinks and turquoise chalky; blend with the lighter coloured pencil instead. Firm burnishing fills the paper tooth, making further layers difficult. Reserve eye reflections as bare paper.

colouringOrder: Inner ears, eyes, mouth and claws
Yellow crown and brown trunk only where visible
